description: Archive each conversation turn to a per-session markdown file in a git repo. Triggers on Stop (right after each assistant turn, for low-latency archiving), SubagentStop (an async subagent / background Task finishes — flushes the conversation even when you've stepped away; the archiver redirects the subagent's sidechain transcript to the main session transcript so subagent prompts/replies are never archived), UserPromptSubmit (a backstop that also captures any multi-message reply blocks flushed to the transcript after Stop fired), and SessionEnd (final turn). The archiver is idempotent — blocks are de-duplicated by message uuid — so the overlapping triggers never produce duplicate content. A SessionStart hook checks runtime dependencies (python3 + git). Session-title changes are reported IMMEDIATELY (not only at turn boundaries) by the lightweight report_title.py on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse — PostToolUse fires after every tool call, so consumers like GenTerminal's sidebar Sessions section see the title within seconds of it changing mid-turn, instead of when the turn ends. A manual /rename outranks the auto-generated ai-title (the two live in different places: the process registry vs the transcript); because /rename fires NO hook, each report_title run also keeps a per-session watcher daemon alive (title_watch.py, POSIX only, ~1.5s stat-fingerprint polls) so a rename made while the session is idle still reaches consumers within seconds instead of at the next prompt — watcher and hook reporter share the last-reported state, so they never double-report, and the watcher exits on its own when the claude process ends. The archive hooks guard on python3 so a missing interpreter is a no-op, never a blocked prompt.

hooks.command: command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/archive.py" || true
